_readme: Places OpenStreetMap doesn't carry, and corrections to places it carries wrongly.
Separate from hours-overlay.json on purpose: that file answers 'when is this open',
this one answers 'does this exist, and where'. Same discipline though — every entry
records where it came from and when it was checked, so a stale entry can be
Applied to public/data/skymap-data.json by scripts/apply-poi-overlay.mjs. Run it
after every `npm run data:osm`, alongside apply-hours-overlay.mjs — extraction
rewrites the dataset and would otherwise drop all of this.
`added` entries sit at their host building's centroid. We don't have a surveyed
point for them and inventing a plausible-looking one would be a fake precision;
the building is the honest answer and the only thing routing needs.
When OSM catches up with an entry, the script reports it as retirable rather than
emitting a duplicate. Retire it then — the upstream record is the better one.
Two independent sources are required before anything lands here, and the operator
wins on conflict. Hotel pages disagree with their own tenants: the Emery listed
Spyhouse as 6:30-5 daily while Spyhouse published 6:30-7 on Wed-Sun.

poi-x-spyhouse-emery.name: Spyhouse Coffee
poi-x-spyhouse-emery.note: The report that started this. Emery already carried Giulia, so a foodless-building sweep would never have found it.

poi-x-aurora-marriott-city-center.name: Aurora Restaurant & Bar
poi-x-aurora-marriott-city-center.note: 5th floor. Hours omitted: Aurora runs three services a day (06:30-10:30, 11:00-16:00, 17:00-23:00) and the app renders one interval per day, so the only recordable form would be 06:30-23:00 — which claims it is open across two gaps it is closed. The Marriott City Center is the building 1.7's feedback said was unmarked; it had no food POI either.
